title: Places and buildings
summary: Rooms, structures and the parts of a town.

questions.clue: This is the room below ground level, often used for storing wine or coal.
questions.note: A basement is usually a habitable floor and a cellar is for storage, but both answer the clue.

questions.clue: This is a large building where goods are kept before they are sold or sent on.
questions.note: The word joins ware, meaning goods for sale, to house. The same root gives us hardware and software.

questions.clue: This is the room where scientists carry out experiments.
questions.note: British English stresses the second syllable and American English the first, which makes it a useful word to hear both ways.

questions.clue: This is the sheltered stretch of water where boats can tie up safely.
questions.note: Harbour is the water itself and a port is the harbour plus everything built around it. Both spellings are accepted.

questions.clue: This is the long narrow passage inside a building with rooms opening off it.
questions.note: Corridor and hallway are the ordinary British and American choices respectively.

questions.clue: This is the residential area on the outer edge of a city, mostly housing.
questions.note: From Latin words meaning under or near the city. The adjective is suburban.

questions.clue: This is the building where university students live, with many small rooms.
questions.note: Dormitory is the American term and halls of residence the British one. From the Latin for sleep.

questions.clue: This is the solid base, built below ground, on which the rest of a building stands.
questions.note: Usually plural when talking about a building. The singular is the one used for an organisation or a principle.

questions.clue: This is the very large church that is the seat of a bishop.
questions.note: From cathedra, the Latin for the bishop's chair. Size is not what makes it one; the bishop is.

questions.clue: This is the large open enclosure with tiered seating where sporting events are held.
questions.note: The plural is stadiums or stadia. An arena is usually roofed and smaller, but it answers the clue.
